nodes.summary: The claim of Kourovka Problem 16.62 is false: there is a group $G$ such that every automorphism of $G$ sends each element $g \in G$ to a conjugate of $g$, but some automorphism of $G$ is not inner, that is, not of the form $x \mapsto h x h^{-1}$ for any $h \in G$.
nodes.title: Groups whose automorphisms all preserve conjugacy classes can have outer automorphisms

nodes.summary: For every group $G$: if every automorphism of $G$ sends each element $g \in G$ to a conjugate of $g$ (equivalently, maps every conjugacy class of $G$ into itself), then every automorphism of $G$ is inner, that is, of the form $x \mapsto h x h^{-1}$ for some $h \in G$.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 16.62

nodes.summary: The claim that for every group $G$, every automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ that sends each element to a conjugate of itself (for each $x \in G$ there is $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$) is inner, that is, there is a single $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$ for all $x \in G$.
nodes.title: Claim of Scottish Book Problem 112

nodes.summary: The claim of Scottish Book Problem 112 is false: there are a group $G$ and an automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ that sends every element to a conjugate of itself (for each $x \in G$ there is $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$) but is not inner (there is no $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$ for all $x \in G$).
nodes.title: Class-preserving automorphisms need not be inner
